title: Green Thai Curry
subtitle: Fragrant Thai chicken curry in green curry paste and coconut milk
excerpt: Chicken thighs in a fragrant coconut milk sauce made with green curry paste, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and fish sauce. Bright, herbal, and deeply aromatic.

recipe.sourceNotes: Thai green curry (gaeng keow wan) is one of the three great Thai curry styles, alongside red and yellow. The green colour comes from the large quantity of fresh green ingredients in the paste: green chillies, lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves and zest, coriander root, and shrimp paste. Green curry is considered the hottest of the three main curries because of the green chillies. In Thailand, the curry is always cooked in a wok over very high heat, beginning by frying the paste in the fat that separates from the coconut milk, before adding the liquid. The vegetables are added last and should retain some texture. The fish sauce provides salting; fresh lime juice at the end provides brightness. Serve with jasmine rice.

content.text: Open the coconut milk without shaking the tin. Spoon the thick cream from the top into the hot pan and cook it until the oil begins to separate and the cream looks slightly curdled and fragrant. This is where the curry paste is fried. Do not add the remaining coconut milk until the paste is cooked in the cream and smells deeply aromatic. The courgette and green beans should retain some bite: add them in the last 5 minutes.

Scoop the thick cream from the top of the unopened coconut milk tin. Heat a large pan over medium-high heat. Add the coconut cream and fry for 2 minutes until the oil separates. Add the green curry paste and lemongrass. Fry for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir to coat. Cook for 3 minutes. Pour in the remaining coconut milk. Add the fish sauce and sugar. Simmer for 12 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.

Add the courgette and green beans. Simmer for 5 minutes until just tender. Remove the lemongrass. Squeeze over the lime juice. Taste: balance fish sauce for salt, lime for acid, sugar for sweetness. Serve with jasmine rice. Top with coriander and sliced chilli.
